questions.q: What does an integration strategy address that building individual integrations well, as taught in course 7, does not?
options: Whether integrations across the enterprise are designed, authenticated, and governed consistently, not just whether any one integration works
How to write a Scripted REST API
How IntegrationHub spokes are licensed
Whether a single integration has correct field mapping
questions.explain: A strategy is about consistency and governance across all integrations, not the technical correctness of any one integration — that was course 7's subject.

options: A list of every scoped application on the instance
A maintained record of every integration touching the instance, including system, pattern, authentication, and owner
A dashboard of REST API response times
A backup of every integration's source code
questions.explain: The inventory is the concrete artifact an integration strategy produces — a record answering what's integrated, how, and who owns it.

questions.q: Why can duplicate integrations happen even when each individual integration is built correctly?
options: Because correctly built integrations are immune to duplication
Because duplication only happens with Basic Auth integrations
Because different teams, months or years apart, may independently connect to the same external system with no inventory to check against first
Because ServiceNow technically prevents more than one integration per external system
questions.explain: Without a shared inventory, there's no way for a second team to discover that a first team already built a connection to the same system.

questions.q: Why is inconsistent authentication across integrations a real enterprise risk, per this lesson?
options: It isn't a risk as long as every integration eventually works
OAuth and Basic Auth perform identically from a risk standpoint
Without an enforced standard, a security review has to audit each integration's authentication individually instead of checking against one documented policy
Inconsistent authentication only affects integration speed, not security
questions.explain: A missing enterprise-wide authentication standard turns a security review into a per-integration audit, since there's no single policy to check compliance against.

questions.q: Under a real integration strategy, when should a new integration get an inventory entry and an owner review, per this lesson?
options: Only after it has been in production for a year
Only if it later causes an incident
Before it's built, so a named owner can review it against the existing inventory
Inventory entries are optional and left to each team's discretion
questions.explain: The strategy requires review before build — catching duplication or an authentication exception early, rather than discovering it after the integration already exists.
